text:
jamie.r: flagging a follow-up to the canary fallback convo. idea: use heartbeat+quorum to trigger soft-switchover rather than raw error-rate thresholds. starting thread to capture pros/cons.

sree.v: love the idea. heartbeat lets us detect gradual degradation earlier. what's the minimum quorum? 2/3 of replicas?

hani.b: for GPU-backed variants replica count varies. quorum should be percent-based (e.g., >=75% healthy) and windowed (30s). also distinguish per-host vs per-variant health.

alice.m: devil's advocate: heartbeats add traffic and complexity. how expensive are these probes? we should reuse existing prediction pings when possible.

jamie.r: agreed we should be frugal. heartbeat = lightweight prefix-check that touches runtime health path without doing full gen. e.g., POST /health/pulse with sample prefix and expected token checksum. cheap and fast.

hani.b: proto heartbeat payload: 
```
POST /health/pulse
{
  "model": "variant-a",
  "prefix": "hello",
  "expect_checksum": "sha256:...",
  "max_latency_ms": 120
}
```

sree.v: router behavior sketch: 1) collect heartbeats across N backends 2) compute rolling healthy_pct 3) if healthy_pct < threshold and errors/spike corroborate -> trigger soft-switchover.

jamie.r: soft-switchover = route new requests to fallback but allow active streams to finish. contrast with hard-switchover which aborts active streams and moves everything.

alice.m: how do we avoid flapping? if variant oscillates we could keep switching. need cooldown, hysteresis, and an operator override.

hani.b: propose cooldown config: cooldown_window=120s, min_stable_window=30s, max_auto_actions_per_hour=3. router enforces these.

sree.v: we also need a prioritized fallback list. sometimes you want to fallback to cheaper quantized variant, sometimes to a smaller context model. order matters.

jamie.r: suggested priority format: [ {name: "v2-quant", reason: "cost-first"}, {name: "v1-stable", reason: "compatibility"} ] and router tries in order until action succeeds.

alice.m: resume compatibility remains sticky. heartbeat should also return "compat_hash" so router can pick fallbacks that are resume-compatible where possible.

hani.b: good call. heartbeat reply fields: status, latency_ms, compat_hash, load_pct. keep it small.

jamie.r: here's a sample router decision table (pseudo): 
``
IF healthy_pct < 75% AND errors.rate > 2% THEN
  for fallback in priority_list:
    if fallback.compat_hash == origin.compat_hash AND fallback.supports_resume:
      action = resume
      break
    else if fallback.supports_stream_proxy:
      action = proxy
      break
  if no action found && allow_restart:
    action = restart
``

sree.v: runtime changes: 1) implement /health/pulse (cheap) 2) return compat_hash + load. 3) expose stream-proxy handshake: /stream/handoff-init body: {session_id, ttl_ms}.

alice.m: for stream-proxy handshake, we need server-signed tokens to prevent spoofing. also rate-limit handoffs to avoid DoS.

hani.b: telemetry: emit events with tags: trigger_type (heartbeat|metric|manual), origin_variant, fallback_variant, action_taken, duration_ms, user_visible_loss (true/false). useful for Optimize.

jamie.r: testing strategy: router simulation with fuzzed heartbeat failures, then a small internal canary of the escape flow using non-critical tenants. validate metrics and rollback ergonomics.

sree.v: ops: add a single-button rollback in console that can 1) revert routing table and 2) abort in-flight proxies (if operator chooses). also allow 'drain-mode' where a variant stops accepting new traffic but finishes streams.

alice.m: security: ensure heartbeats don't leak model tokens or internal prompt samples. use synthetic prefixes and checksum-only validation.

hani.b: long-term: surface a 'compatibility registry' in control plane where model owners can declare compat guarantees (resume-safe, tokenizer-stable). router can consult registry before fallback.

jamie.r: outstanding questions: - metric thresholds: who owns defaults? product or infra? - how to bill when streams finish on old node while new ones go to fallback? - multi-tenant noisy neighbor isolates?

sree.v: answers: defaults by infra but overrideable by product/tenant. billing: tag sessions with origin_variant and fallback_variant; billing pipeline charges per actual host usage. noisy neighbors: policy scoping by tenant and host.

alice.m: next steps: hani will draft health/pulse API and compat_hash spec. sree will prototype router-quorum logic in the simulator. jamie will write short RFC w/ decision table and test plan. i'll file the canary runbook.

ops-bot: task created CANARY-SWITCH-2026 assigned to jamie.r, sree.v, hani.b, alice.m. smoke-date: 2026-04-15.

jamie.r: thanks all — will sync after RFC.
